---
title: "HIV Surveillance Manager CI Investigation"
date: 2026-09-22
date-modified: 2026-09-23
---

**Status:** Evidence-backed investigation. Merge-path isolation, a focused path
check, and a manual-only hosted section-to-final trial workflow are on
`jheem_analyses` `master`. The five observed sections are preserved as a
versioned release snapshot. The first hosted trial exposed a missing runtime
package after a partial build; a corrected manual retry is in progress. No
validated hosted candidate or runner-margin conclusion exists yet. This is not
a raw-to-final automation or promotion claim.

**Verified against:** `jheem_analyses@16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3`
on 2026-09-22. A read-only shared-storage inventory on the same date confirmed
five section files and the current final manager. File sizes, timestamps,
serialized object names, and SHA-256 digests were checked; this does not establish
that these files were built as one coherent release or that they reproduce the
current manager under the current code.
The input and path changes described below were rechecked on 2026-09-23;
merge-path implementation is pinned to `jheem_analyses@0cd67c0`; the manual
trial workflow began at `jheem_analyses@cc2b9e1` and its dependency correction
is `jheem_analyses@670dd92`.

## Current build boundary

Five [section scripts](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/data_processing/hiv.surveillance.manager/hiv.surveillance.processing.for.merging)
produce `surveillance.manager_section1.rdata` through
`surveillance.manager_section5.rdata`. They source data-processing scripts and
write section files into a shared-drive merge directory. The scripts and their
sourced processors read raw inputs from shared-drive paths, while section 1 also
loads a census manager from the local `cached/` directory. These are not yet
declared, immutable CI inputs; changing only the top-level section output paths
would not make raw-to-section builds portable.

The [merge script](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/data_processing/hiv.surveillance.manager/hiv.surveillance.processing.for.merging/hiv.surveillance.manager.merge.R#L11-L60)
loads those five files, imports sections 2, 4, 3, and 5 into section 1, then
sources aggregation, STI-ratio, HIV-testing, MSM-proportion, outlier-removal,
and Oakland-specific processing. It saves a pre-outlier copy, a final local
`surveillance.manager.rdata`, a shared-drive current copy, and a date-stamped
archive copy. The sourced processing scripts include further census-manager
loads from both `../../cached/` and `Q:/data_managers/`, repository-relative
`source()` calls into `jheem2`, and an Oakland migration step that reads raw
county-to-county flow files from `Q:/data_raw/`. The candidate build therefore
needs to isolate *all* merge-time inputs and outputs, not only the five initial
`load.data.manager()` calls. See the
[aggregation script](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/data_processing/hiv.surveillance.manager/hiv.surveillance.processing.for.merging/updated.data.aggregation.jheem.R#L1-L7)
and [migration input](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/data_processing/hiv.surveillance.manager/tga_migration.R#L38-L45).

### Observed artifact set (2026-09-22)

| Artifact | Size | Last file modification | Outcomes |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Section 1 | 19.0 MiB | 2026-08-26 | 9 |
| Section 2 | 9.1 MiB | 2026-08-26 | 15 |
| Section 3 | 1.0 MiB | 2026-08-24 | 5 |
| Section 4 | 9.5 MiB | 2026-08-26 | 5 |
| Section 5 | 1.1 MiB | 2026-05-13 | 8 |
| Current final manager | 42.4 MiB | 2026-08-31 | 42 |

The five sections contain 39 distinct outcome names; merge-time processing
produces three additional outcomes: `gonorrhea.ratio`, `ps.syphilis.ratio`, and
`hiv.tests.per.population`. The dates differ, notably for section 5. That may be
intentional reuse of unchanged inputs, but a directory listing is not an
atomic-build manifest. The current manager has the same SHA-256 digest as its
August 31 archive copy. Against the August 26 archive manager, the generic
structural validator reports no missing structure in the August 31 manager and
three additional locations (`C.29820`, `C.31080`, `C.41740`) for each of the
`cocaine` and `heroin` NSDUH outcomes. This comparison does not check data values.

The Oakland post-processing step reads 24 county-to-county migration workbooks
covering 12 time windows. Together they occupy about 1.5 GiB on shared storage.
The first CI design must either make those exact raw files available to a hosted
runner or execute the candidate build on a suitably isolated runner with
read-only access to them. The five small section files are not sufficient by
themselves.

### Release-backed input path (verified 2026-09-22)

The existing
[`data-raw-v2026.08.24` release](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/data-raw-v2026.08.24)
has a `data-raw-movement.tar.gz` asset (1,230,758,289 bytes; published SHA-256
`e5db3f70c21d95962a2d4a1725a8ee5e55aede975573ce3642fa36d8229acbfe`).
The [uploader](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/scripts/upload_raw_data.R)
archives the entire `data_raw/movement/` subdirectory. On 2026-09-23, all 24
county-to-county workbooks read by the local merge matched the released archive
byte-for-byte. The
[`data-managers-v2026.08.26` release](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/data-managers-v2026.08.26)
contains a 108,009,923-byte census manager whose published SHA-256
(`f8c710684ccfdfb3a5c8e6f4b54caf0417ab67afb82b89ab3259c4b8151e1053`)
matches the NAS copy used in the successful local merge. The five observed HIV
section files were subsequently preserved together in a release snapshot. Their
different modification dates are not source lineage.

### Five-section snapshot and hosted trial (2026-09-23)

The [HIV section snapshot release](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/hiv-sections-snapshot-2026.09.23)
contains the five NAS-observed section files and a `SHA256SUMS.txt` manifest.
The uploaded bytes and GitHub asset digests were verified against the observed
files. The release records a *snapshot of merge inputs*, not evidence that the
five sections came from one raw-data build, nor a rebuild from the release's
target commit. It did not change the active manager or any `latest` alias.

[`jheem_analyses@cc2b9e1`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/cc2b9e1)
adds a [manual-only hosted trial](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/cc2b9e1/.github/workflows/trial-hiv-surveillance-manager.yml).
It checks out exact analyses, jheem2, and locations revisions; downloads the
five-section snapshot, the movement archive, a dated census manager, and a
dated surveillance baseline by digest; builds a candidate with shared writes
disabled; measures Linux memory and disk use; and uploads the candidate and
evidence as a short-lived Actions artifact. Its structural comparison is
provisional: it does not constitute an active-model consumer or selected-value
gate. The workflow neither publishes a candidate release nor promotes an active
manager. The [first trial run](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/35851080701)
completed input verification, then failed late in the merge because the workflow
had not installed `tidyverse`, which a sourced processor loads. It produced a
pre-outlier manager but no final candidate. The partial run took 24 minutes in
the merge step and reached 8,178,336 KiB peak resident memory; neither number
is a completed-build benchmark. [`670dd92`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/670dd92)
adds the direct runtime packages and checks that they load *before* the merge.
The [manual retry](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/35854104948)
must complete before drawing a runner-capacity or candidate-quality conclusion.

Because `jheem_analyses` is public, GitHub's current standard Ubuntu runner has
16 GB RAM and 14 GB storage and is free for public-repository workflows
([runner specifications](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)).
The observed local process reached about 10 GiB of resident memory, but a macOS
measurement cannot certify the Linux peak or disk footprint. A selective
hosted-runner trial is therefore the first sizing check. Downloading every raw
archive in the syphilis workflow would add unrelated data and should not be
copied into this job.

### Merge-path isolation (2026-09-23)

[`jheem_analyses@0cd67c0`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/0cd67c0)
lets the section-to-final merge take explicit section, two census-manager,
county-to-county workbook, and candidate-output paths. With
`WRITE_SHARED_OUTPUT=false`, it requires all five path settings and skips the
legacy shared current and archive writes. Omitting the new settings preserves
the existing `Q:`/`cached/` workflow. The
[focused path check](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/0cd67c0/data_processing/hiv.surveillance.manager/test_merge_paths.R)
covers both modes and rejects incomplete candidate configuration without
loading manager data. The earlier full local merge used the same path-routing
changes, but the full data build was not rerun after this commit's added
fail-closed configuration check. This is an enabling code change, not a CI build
or a claim of a supported candidate path.

An isolated local merge probe on 2026-09-22, using the observed sections,
census manager, and migration inputs with shared writes disabled, completed a
candidate build. It surfaced a runtime dependency: installed `locations`
0.4.0 rejected the current code's `include.partial` argument, while
[`locations` 0.5.0.9000 at `2481fc44`](https://github.com/tfojo1/locations/tree/2481fc440cf1d981bb1005dd903708a88a528d13)
completed the merge. A comparison with the active August 31 manager found
identical `data` content across all 408 nested arrays and no structural
differences in either direction across 603 generic spec checks. The R6 outcome
metadata compared equal by value; the `last.modified.date` differed, as did
the serialized file digest. This is strong evidence that the current merge path
can reproduce the active manager's data from these inputs, but it does not
recover the original build's code and package identities or validate scientific
fitness of the values. The R process used approximately 10 GiB of resident
memory after 14 minutes; the pre-outlier and final artifacts were written more
than 30 minutes apart. CI needs explicit package pins and a measured runner
budget.

The current
[syphilis-manager hosted workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/build-syphilis-manager.yml)
is a useful partial template: it downloads prebuilt section files and other
dependencies, assembles and structurally validates a manager, and creates a
versioned release. Its raw-data-to-section stage is not part of that hosted
workflow. The separate syphilis section workflow has no recorded runs as of the
earlier audit. The generic
[manager-spec validation tools](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/data_processing/validation)
could support an HIV baseline, but the repository documents a surveillance
validation directory as future work rather than an existing checked-in spec.
Prebuilt surveillance and census managers are already distributed together as
`data-managers-v*` dependency snapshots by
[`scripts/upload_manager_deps.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/scripts/upload_manager_deps.R);
that snapshots an existing manager rather than building one in CI.

## Candidate first increment

The first CI claim should be narrow: **given an identified set of five section
artifacts and identified auxiliary inputs, assemble an HIV surveillance manager
on a GitHub-hosted runner, check it, and publish a versioned candidate**.
Promotion to the active manager remains a separate action.

1. Preserve the exact five section inputs together with sizes and digests,
   documenting known and unknown upstream lineage. The 2026-09-23 snapshot
   completes this input handoff; its manifest digest, not a mutable shared-drive
   path or `latest` alias, identifies the build input.
2. Pin the analyses, `jheem2`, `locations`, and runtime versions used by the
   hosted job. Keep the now-isolated merge transformations unchanged.
3. Build a reviewed structural baseline from a known-good surveillance manager.
   Validate outcome/source/ontology/stratification shape and selected values or
   queries used by active consumers. The syphilis build is one downstream
   consumer of the HIV surveillance manager; a suitable compatibility probe
   should cover that boundary as well as an active HIV-model use where feasible.
4. Download only the required release assets to a temporary workspace on a
   hosted runner. Measure peak memory, disk, download/install time, and merge
   duration on Linux before deciding that the standard runner is sufficient.
   Produce a candidate artifact, build log, input identities, validation report,
   and output digest. Review the candidate before any `latest` alias or shared
   current-file update.

This would give contributors a repeatable verdict on changes to the merge and
post-processing stages. It would **not** yet prove that each section can be
recreated from raw surveillance files in CI. The raw-to-section stages can be
made portable and automated incrementally after their inputs and runtime costs
are known.

## Open questions and destination

- Were the five snapshotted sections the inputs to the current August 31
  manager? Their bytes are now preserved, but the original raw-to-section
  source revisions and build lineage remain unproved.
- Which merge-time `source()` calls read additional inputs or write intermediate
  files? The top-level script audit is not a complete side-effect audit.
- Which active HIV-model queries and syphilis-build dependencies constitute a
  useful consumer compatibility check? Structural equality alone cannot answer
  whether a changed value remains scientifically suitable.
- Does the selective section-to-final merge fit the public repository's standard
  hosted runner with sufficient memory, disk, and time margin? If not, what
  measured stage should be optimized or isolated before considering a larger or
  self-hosted runner? A runner with NAS access must not execute arbitrary,
  unreviewed changes from contributors.

Build scripts, fixtures, validation specs, and runnable instructions should
graduate into `jheem_analyses` with the workflow they protect. Retire this
investigation when that repository documents the supported build boundary and
its CI has completed a candidate build with identified inputs and a reviewed
validation result.
